children: Shilpa Samant New Delhi: The power ministry is considering a plan to extend Section 11 provisions for imported coal-based Mundra power plant that will require the unit to run at full capacity till December amid elevated power demand, people aware of the development said. The Tata Power-owned 4,000 MW plant is currently operating under the special provisions, slated to end this month.

The government is likely to extend the plant's requirement further under the provisions in view of persistent high domestic power demand, the people said. The directive will be issued under Section 11 of the Electricity Act, which provides that the Centre may in extraordinary circumstances ask a power generation company to operate and maintain any station in line with its directions, the people said.

The Mundra plant has a supplemental power purchase agreement (SPPA) with Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Ltd, and discussions are also on with Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab and Maharashtra. "Discussions with Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab to sign SPPAs are at an advanced stage," said one of the persons cited above.

The Mundra plant requires a SPPA to allow a full passthrough of volatile imported coal costs and make the capacity available for supply. Peak power demand in the country crossed the projected 271 GW in September, unusually high for the month, led by cooling and irrigation demand following a deficit monsoon. Thermal plants play a key role in meeting high power demand, especially in non-solar hours. The projected peak was at 271 GW this year, higher than last year's summer peak of 243 GW. The power ministry didn't respond to an email query. The cost of imported coal-based power plants is usually higher than those running on domestic fuel.

title: Mundra Plant May Get Nod to Run Full Throttle Till December
